project.purpose: Own one bounded Agent Run's durable cognition, provider/tool interaction, action admission, effect binding, recovery, and completion proposal without owning caller Task meaning or Runtime physical truth.

nodes.label: RunContract
nodes.responsibility: Bind one exact Harness Run contract, provider/tool affordances, budgets, and caller context.
acceptance: A run is independently identifiable and bounded.
Run Trace evidence must use exact integer event/version/time/clock fields, string Run identity, and an immutable tuple of events; numeric aliases are rejected at the native consumer boundary.

nodes.label: ContextProjection
nodes.responsibility: Compile current model cognition from durable working set, current ingress, and attempt context rather than replaying complete history.
acceptance: Context can be rebuilt from bounded owned sources.

nodes.label: ActionAdmission
nodes.responsibility: Turn model/tool proposals into exact admitted actions without treating intent as authority.
acceptance: Unadmitted proposals cannot become tool effects.
Bounded native TLC Provider claim admission model checks a current claimant generation and expiry replacement before physical dispatch. Executable SQLite refinement is independently scoped.

PG WakeTurn admission clocks are exact nonnegative PostgreSQL signed 64-bit integers (type(value) is int and value <= 2**63-1); bool/float/string aliases and overflow fail closed with a typed domain conflict before the durable insert, with native PG counterexamples, independently of the legacy SQLite source.

nodes.label: EffectBinding
nodes.responsibility: Bind admitted tool intents to physical evidence while preserving ambiguous-effect semantics.
acceptance: Lost response does not cause blind duplicate effect.
Live A/B MemoryRuntime H04 fixture admits only exact requestId-to-digest replay, disjoint edit intervals, and one producer per file; malformed requests cannot emit a successful effect receipt.

Temporal Worker deployment derives four exact runtime package versions solely from the installed requirements freeze, rejects stale/invalid source projections, and evaluates runtimeVersionsExact using one observed interpreter state per Plan.
Finite model separates at-most-one physical Provider effect, durable result, ambiguous outcome and caller acknowledgement. Live delivery is not entailed by TLC PASS.

Durable ConversationRelay SQLite materialization transitions validate the exact post-write receipt before COMMIT; missing or malformed readback must ROLLBACK and fail with CarrierConflict. This contract holds for intent, effect attempt, ordinary outcome, and human-resume claim under Python -O, without claiming external provider atomicity.

A durable Provider completion digest is not caller acknowledgement: native TLC must prove acknowledgement requires fresh or privacy-authorized retained result, and metadata-only redaction remains independently reachable. Concrete SQLite replay/recovery tests and the separately merged #668 12-worker consumer remain required; bounded model PASS alone does not prove implementation refinement.

The Python -O qualification requires executable, non-elided SQL-state postconditions for adverse receipt markers and persisted row standings; two deliberately unequal witnesses must still raise AssertionError in both optimized and standard interpreters. A pytest exit-zero without these checks is not durable receipt proof.

A CFT human-session open must prove the exact durable OPENING reservation receipt inside its SQLite transaction before any systemd.start: deleted or mutated post-insert reservation rolls back and no physical browser start/stop is attempted. Native SQLite adversarial AFTER INSERT triggers cover deleted rows and wrong slot; external browser readiness and deployed installed state require separate evidence. The OPENING-to-ACTIVE transition must additionally prove exact durable ACTIVE receipt after physical readiness, or roll back and compensate the started systemd target rather than return a false READY.

After systemd.stop of an existing human-session, the CFT CLOSED transition must affect the exact selected lifecycle and preserve all immutable session identity fields with an exact closedAtMs. Native SQLite post-UPDATE row removal or reactivation must ROLLBACK and raise SessionConflict, never emit a successful CLOSED receipt; this source invariant does not make systemd.stop and the SQLite write one atomic physical transaction.

Conversation-role adoption and wake-intent Turn identity allocation require exact, typed, post-write SQLite receipt readback before COMMIT; a missing or tampered row must roll back with owner Conflict and must not commit any trigger side effect. Exact replays cannot return a forged provider/session or invalid UUIDv7 turn identity. The physical test scope is the two original SQLite stores, not external provider SEND atomicity.

The Browserless turn-effect SQLite read-only reconciliation path must close its native sqlite3.Connection exactly once for both existing row and absent-table cases; SQLite transaction context is not a connection-lifetime owner. A real tracked sqlite3.Connection subclass is the negative/positive resource oracle; this does not close unrelated connections in other callers.

Until HarnessStore has a PostgreSQL-backed replacement qualified by the same lease, revision, event and receipt consumer tests, SQLite backup verification must bind exact filename identity: reserved #/?/% are physical bytes, never query or fragment syntax; valid-but-wrong database aliases must fail consumer equivalence.

PostgreSQL-first cutover acceptance is consumer equivalence for run/event CAS, leases, unique dedupe and provider receipts under serializable retry, independent data restoration/rollback, production readback and retirement of superseded SQLite authority; a connector or schema alone is not migration.

Migration-source identity: existing Agent Automation Release must snapshot and copy the exact SQLite ledger path through standard-library URI encoding. A literal '#' in a filename or ancestor directory cannot redirect the read to another valid database, and a corrupted named source must never pass by alias. This is interim SQLite source integrity, not PostgreSQL migration completion.

PostgreSQL-first WakeTurn identity cutover: a wakeIntentId maps to exactly one immutable UUIDv7 turnRequestId under native PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE retry. A previously populated SQLite wake source may be retired only after a quiesced, exclusive-source-lock import proves row-by-row equivalence and installs exact INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE fail-closed triggers. Browserless may use PG only on an explicit DSN, after validating the source seal plus legacy-to-PG identity equality; a missing source requires explicitly qualified fresh bootstrap. Failure must hold without SQLite fallback or provider SEND. This source-level/native PostgreSQL evidence does not prove already-running legacy workers have stopped or an installed deployment has switched.

PostgreSQL WakeTurn first-schema admission is a single serialized database capability: a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock precedes CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE; on an empty disposable database 12-way cold initialization succeeds without pg_namespace UniqueViolation and creates exactly one schema/table.

Native PostgreSQL WakeTurn first-admission schema is not certified by CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alone: existing relation must be a plain table with the exact six typed nonnull columns, an immutable wake primary key, a nondeferrable unique turn identity and a nonnegative BIGINT timestamp check. The PostgreSQL cutover marker also requires a plain two-column non-RLS table with an enforced nondeferrable PRIMARY KEY and exact CHECK constraints on cutover_id='legacy' and state in {'PENDING','ACTIVE'}, preventing counterfeit identity or state transitions. Disposable PostgreSQL tests falsify an existing same-named table missing unique turn identity, using a wrong timestamp type or missing its check, or a cutover marker table missing its primary key; incomplete schema rejects before any WakeTurn write. This only qualifies the current admission transaction and does not establish arbitrary future DDL noninterference or complete SQLite-to-PostgreSQL cutover.

H04 PostgreSQL ConversationBinding replacement is independently source-path-bound. One existing Browserless consumer selects the same PG store for exact read and adoption; unsealed legacy sources fail closed at both the consumer and direct PG API. PG SERIALIZABLE + exact post-write receipt and source-retired one-time import have 8 disposable-PostgreSQL physical tests, including replay, concurrency, mutation rollback and legacy-after-PG-growth non-vacuity; 4 no-fallback Browserless CDC tests. This proves neither deployed PG cutover nor Runtime/Harness-wide SQLite retirement.

After PostgreSQL WakeTurn identity admission, the native PostgreSQL owner must reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE of the persisted wake identity row, rather than rely only on Agent-side post-write reads. Real PostgreSQL 18 negative controls must show all three illegal mutation/erase attempts fail and the original turn UUIDv7 remains unchanged. Privileged trigger disabling, direct file corruption and DROP TABLE are outside this scoped contract and require owner-role/privilege boundaries; the ProviderClaimR1 abstract TLC result is not a PG implementation refinement proof.

PostgreSQL conversation-binding PG native CHECKs preserve the exact legacy accepted campaignRef (nonempty trimmed text) rather than imposing an unproven SHA-256 prefix on existing valid identity; physical PostgreSQL RED/green import of campaign:historic-role must preserve replay with UUIDv7 session, SHA-256 evidence/binding digests and BIGINT checks intact.

PostgreSQL 18 ConversationBinding schema admission must bind exact native named primary/unique/createdAtMs/digest/UUIDv7 constraint definitions from pg_constraint; keyword-bearing or same-name weak CHECK expressions cannot stand in for the Owner schema. In disposable real PG18, both anonymous and counterfeit-named weak CHECKs are deliberately rejected. This is a bounded native PG structural contract, not proof of deployed PG configuration, schema owner roles, privilege isolation, historical cutover or external effects.

H04 Capability LEGO: the existing PG ConversationBinding owner and real Browserless read/write consumers; Method LEGO: finite cutover state-machine + CEGAR counterexamples, using Runtime's public upstream TLA+/TLC tool. Native gate verifies PG import and old writer seal are separate states, never admits PG before sealing, preserves legacy IDs across interrupted migration, and permits replay with PG-only growth. Three deliberately false reachability properties prove that admitted PG, interrupted import, and post-growth replay are reachable. A model PASS alone is not installed-PG or SQL transaction proof.

nodes.label: RuntimeToolRequestLowering
nodes.responsibility: Translate an admitted model-facing Runtime tool call into an exact native Runtime operation and JSON request while preserving fixed execution binding, Tool Grant path/execution constraints and replay-safe external request identity; multiple existing bridges consume this shared lowering.
nodes.authority: Harness tool-call translation only; does not grant Runtime execution, access, credentials or physical effects
acceptance: Actual lower_runtime_tool uses HarnessExecutionBinding, explicit Tool Grant and known Job/Artifact references; forbidden path, unsupported arguments and non-conforming request types are rejected rather than broadened.
Two existing concrete consumer adapters invoke the shared translation instead of silently redefining operation schemas.
Changing the exact lowering source changes the source-membership impact of H07; a passing unit test does not imply installed Runtime effect acceptance.
inputs: RuntimeToolGrantView, known Job IDs and Artifact references
outputs: Runtime operation name, canonical native request payload and optional external request identity, or ToolBridgeError
nodes.behavioralContract: For admitted tool-call families, lower only caller-bound Runtime operations and exact typed request shapes. Preserve workspace identity and deterministic clientRequestId from the original binding; reject unsupported arguments, unauthorized path/exec permissions and missing required referenced facts. Translation itself is effect-opaque and does not independently grant execution.
environment: Harness Python source code; actual Gateway/Runtime installed identity and authorization remain external
effects: Construct and validate request only; no direct process execution or state mutation

nodes.label: CognitionMutationAdmission
nodes.responsibility: Admit exact proposed WorkingSet mutation or caller-ingress promotion only against current selected cognition and an explicitly installed handler, independently of projecting the model's next context.
nodes.authority: Harness cognition mutation admission only; durable WorkingSet persistence belongs to supplied handlers and continuity verification
mustNotOwn: durable WorkingSet persistence or Host work authority
acceptance: A proposal cannot mutate a cognition surface absent an installed handler; an old source WorkingSet digest is rejected rather than silently promoting stale state.
Caller-ingress promotion and ordinary WorkingSet transition remain different actions and return committed selection-change facts.
Existing loop and native test consumers exercise both positive and negative admission, without a claim that all installed Agent clients consume the kernel.
inputs: expected source WorkingSet digest and model-view digest, installed handler
outputs: CognitionAdmission carrying source/committed WorkingSet and selection_changed, or typed rejection
nodes.behavioralContract: Validate the requested cognition mutation surface exists and source digest matches currently selected WorkingSet before invoking a supplied persistence handler. No implicit handler grant or stale transition is permitted; different mutation classes keep distinct evidence/progress semantics.
environment: Harness Python Loop with explicitly supplied WorkingSet/caller-ingress handlers; installed consumer coverage not asserted
effects: Calls delegated approved WorkingSet handler only after current-source qualification; does not itself own durable state
